cells.quote: In the control group, anxiety increased from Baseline during the Intervention phase (β = 0.43, 95% HPD [0.25, 0.61]) and remained elevated in the Post phase (β = 0.30, 95% HPD [0.08, 0.50]). In the breathwork group, boredom stayed near Baseline during the Intervention phase (β = 0.02, 95% HPD [−0.10, 0.14]) and remained close to Baseline in the Post phase (β = 0.07, 95% HPD [−0.08, 0.20]).

O.outcome_detail: anxiety at learning-proximal versus end-of-day assessments

cells.quote: In contrast, the breathwork group showed lower anxiety at learning-proximal moments relative to 20:00 (β = −0.20, 95% HPD [−0.31, −0.09]). The between-group difference in this contrast was credible (β = −0.17, 95% HPD [−0.33, −0.01]), indicating that the anxiety-reducing benefit of breathwork was acute and time-specific: anxiety was selectively reduced during the learning-proximal window, but this effect did not fully generalize to the end-of-day context.

O.outcome_detail: enjoyment across learning-proximal and end-of-day assessments

cells.quote: During the Intervention phase, both groups showed modestly higher enjoyment at learning-proximal moments relative to 20:00, but estimates were uncertain (control: β = 0.06; breathwork: β = 0.09) and the between-group difference was not credible (β = 0.03, 95% HPD [−0.15, 0.21]). Thus, there was no clear evidence that breathwork altered the within-day trajectory of enjoyment.
cells.note: This is coded ns, not 0, because the study reports uncertainty but no equivalence test or adequate-power claim.
